market_notes: LENS 1 (content/affiliate/newsletter/data): Sponsorship pricing for sub-5k lists is a flat $50-$300 per placement (destinicopp.com, paved.com), so a newsletter started on Day 1 with zero list cannot plausibly produce sponsorship revenue by Day 45; content plays must instead be "intent tools" (calculators, alert services) that monetize the first users directly via affiliate payouts or a small paid tier. Canadian fintech affiliates are unusually rich (Wealthsimple affiliate: 5% per sale / up to $1,250 per funded client per getlasso.co and promotions.wealthsimple.com), which makes small Canadian-specific calculator sites viable even at low traffic, but approval and SEO lag put first revenue at 30-60 days. Alert/data products built on free government feeds (IRCC Express Entry draws, CanadaBuys tenders) have proven paid competitors (TraceCA lifetime tier with 2,807 users claimed; GovBids $19-$79/mo) and can charge from week 2-3, though the tender-alert space already has 4+ indie entrants. No evidence was found on calculator-site revenue post AI Overviews; treat all traffic assumptions as unverified. LENS 2 (e-commerce/POD): TikTok Shop is NOT available in Canada as of mid-2026 (atlanticworks.ca, rubylegal.ai), Redbubble now takes a 50% platform fee from Standard-tier artists since Sept 2025 (help.redbubble.com, lavaritte.com), and KDP publishers earn $0-$30/month in their first 6 months (kdpeasy.com, zonguru.com). Printify via Etsy with Canadian print providers gives 30-50% margins and 4-8 day domestic shipping (merchize.com, printify.com), and Etsy's own trend reports confirm personalization demand (etsy.com seller handbook, Q4 2025 buyer growth). No source gave a median time-to-first-sale for new Etsy shops; every estimate here is an assumption. Net: POD/KDP can produce a first sale in 2-6 weeks but Day-90 revenue is small and margin after Etsy/Amazon fees is thin; only the personalized-Etsy candidate has a realistic path to a few hundred CAD by Day 90. LENS 3 (marketplaces/directories/lead-gen): Job boards and directories show real solo-operator income (Real Work From Anywhere >$5k MRR, SaaSHub $99/mo featured x108 = >$10k MRR, OpenAlternative $3-3.5k/mo) but the chicken-and-egg lag is severe: RWFA took years to its first paid listing (indiehackers.com), and early-stage boards sell 1-3 listings/month at $99-$199 (jakeinsight.com, jobboardly.com). Inbound lead-gen has the strongest willingness to pay: Canadian contractors already pay HomeStars C$40-80 per shared lead plus $200-500/mo subscriptions and rate it 2.7/5 (leadtruffle.co, smartcustomer.com, BBB), so an exclusive-lead niche RFQ site has a clear value proposition, but it depends on SEO or small ad spend to generate homeowner requests and on the owner setting up an ads account. All three lens-3 candidates are plausible for a first dollar by Day 30-45 only if the supply side is seeded from public data (ATS feeds, public listings) so the site is useful before the first paying customer.

candidates.name: Canadian Money Tools (FHSA/TFSA/RRSP intent calculators + Wealthsimple/EQ affiliate)
candidates.one_liner: A small site of Canada-specific personal-finance calculators (FHSA contribution room, TFSA room by birth year, RRSP-vs-TFSA, 2026 mortgage stress test) monetized by Canadian fintech affiliate payouts.
candidates.target_customer: Canadians aged 20-40 checking FHSA/TFSA/RRSP room and comparing accounts before opening one (Wealthsimple, EQ Bank).
candidates.problem: Government pages explain rules but do not compute a person's room or compare accounts; existing calculator sites are US-centric or bank-owned.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Free calculators; revenue from Wealthsimple affiliate (5% per sale / up to $1,250 per funded client) and EQ Bank referral bonuses; optional CAD 9 'export my plan' PDF later.
candidates.first_10_customers: First 10 affiliate conversions from Reddit r/PersonalFinanceCanada answers that link the calculator only where subreddit rules allow tool links, plus long-tail SEO for 'FHSA contribution room calculator 2026' style queries.
candidates.first_100_customers: Programmatic pages per year-of-birth/province (TFSA room tables), Pinterest pins of the charts, and inclusion in Canadian finance Discord/Reddit wikis; 100 funded referrals is a Day-120+ outcome, not Day-90.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Canada-specific 2026 limits, no login, no bank bias; the affiliate payout per funded account is large enough that a few hundred monthly visitors can pay for the site.

evidence.claim: Wealthsimple affiliate program pays 5% per sale and a referral marketing fee up to $1,250 when a client opens and funds an account within 30 days.
Wealthsimple's own affiliate referral program page confirms compensation is tied to a Promotion Account opened via tracked link and funded within 30 days.
EQ Bank runs a referral program with bonuses up to $500 (customer referral, not a formal affiliate rate).
Calculator pages will earn organic clicks despite AI Overviews; no case study found either way.

candidates.gross_margin_est: 90%+ (hosting near zero; affiliate payouts net of nothing)
candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner registers domain and applies to Wealthsimple/EQ affiliate programs (identity, tax info) in setup block; nothing weekly.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Affiliate approval delayed or denied for a brand-new site, and SEO traffic too slow inside 90 days.
key_risks: Affiliate program may require established traffic before approval
AI Overviews absorb simple 'what is my TFSA room' queries
Reddit self-promotion rules limit distribution
Payout lag: funded-account conversions may post after Day 90
candidates.why_now_2026: FHSA is still new (2023) and 2026 limits/mortgage rules changed, creating fresh query demand; Canadian fintech affiliate payouts are at record highs while US-centric calculator sites ignore Canada.

candidates.name: DrawWatch: Express Entry / PNP draw alerts with CRS-threshold push and history API
candidates.one_liner: Free draw alerts plus a one-time paid tier that pushes instantly (email/Telegram/Discord) when a draw meets the user's category and CRS score, backed by a public JSON API of draw history.
candidates.model_type: freemium data/alert product (one-time or annual fee)
candidates.target_customer: Express Entry and PNP candidates (hundreds of thousands in the pool) and small immigration consultants tracking draws for clients.
candidates.problem: IRCC's free emails are generic; candidates want to know within minutes whether THEIR score/category was drawn and what the trend implies.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Free basic alerts; CAD 19 lifetime or CAD 4/mo for personalized threshold alerts, category tracking and history dashboards; CAD 29/mo API tier for consultants.
candidates.first_10_customers: Organic posts/answers in immigration subreddits and Discord servers where tool links are permitted, and SEO pages 'latest Express Entry draw' auto-updated within minutes of each draw.
candidates.first_100_customers: Ranking for per-category draw pages (CEC, French, healthcare) and referral links from users; consultants discover the API via the public history pages.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Personalized threshold alerts and a machine-readable history API; TraceCA proves paid demand but offers only generic alerts.

evidence.claim: TraceCA sells 'lifetime access for unlimited future alerts' on top of free email alerts and claims 2,807 applicants have used it.
IRCC offers free generic Express Entry email updates, setting the free baseline the paid tier must beat.
Multiple consultancies (canadim.com, immigration.ca) publish draw trackers, indicating high search demand for draw results.
Conversion of free alert users to a CAD 19 tier at 2-3% is assumed, not measured.

candidates.gross_margin_est: 90%+ (Stripe fees only; scraping of public IRCC pages is free)
candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner sets up Stripe and domain once; all draw ingestion, alerts and support FAQs are automated.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Free alternatives (IRCC email, X accounts, consultancy pages) are good enough and users will not pay even CAD 19.
key_risks: Immigration subreddits restrict promotional links
Draw frequency is irregular so value is episodic
Consultancy sites dominate SEO for draw queries
Must not present as immigration advice (regulated in Canada)
candidates.why_now_2026: Category-based draws (French, healthcare, trades) multiplied in 2025-2026, making generic alerts less useful and score/category-specific alerts more valuable.

candidates.name: SmallBid: SMB-sized Canadian public tender alerts (CanadaBuys + provincial portals) with AI summaries
candidates.one_liner: A vertical-specific tender alert and digest service for small Canadian service firms (e.g., janitorial, landscaping, IT services under $100k) built on free CanadaBuys open data.
candidates.target_customer: Canadian small service businesses (1-20 staff) who could bid on small federal/provincial contracts but do not pay MERX.
candidates.problem: CanadaBuys is free but noisy; MERX charges $15-$160/mo; owners want only the small contracts in their trade, summarized in plain language.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Free weekly digest; CAD 15/mo per trade vertical with daily alerts, AI summaries and deadline calendar; CAD 39/mo multi-vertical.
candidates.first_10_customers: SEO pages per trade and province ('janitorial tenders Ontario') and posts in Canadian small-business communities where tool sharing is allowed; free tier converts to paid when a relevant tender appears.
candidates.first_100_customers: Programmatic coverage of every trade x province, a public 'awarded contracts' dataset that earns links, and referrals from bookkeepers/associations.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Cheaper and narrower than MERX/Biddingo; unlike GovBids (general), it is filtered to small-value contracts a micro-business can actually win.

evidence.claim: GovBids sells CanadaBuys-derived alerts at $19/$39/$79 per month, claiming ~80% less than MERX's $30-$160/mo; data refreshed every 2 hours.
MERX entry plan is approximately CAD 14.95/mo (early 2026) or $70/document; CanadaBuys itself is free.
At least four indie aggregators (GovBid, GovBids, BidFit, Jorpex) already compete on this data.
Small service firms will pay CAD 15/mo for a narrowed feed; conversion rates not found.

candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner sets up Stripe/domain; ingestion, summaries and billing are fully automated.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Crowded with recent indie clones of the same free data; differentiation by vertical may not overcome buyer inertia.
key_risks: CanadaBuys data licence terms must be respected
Provincial portals vary and some restrict scraping
Small firms rarely bid; low activation
Churn after first unsuccessful bid
candidates.why_now_2026: CanadaBuys fully replaced BuyandSell and publishes open data; cheap LLM summarization makes plain-language, trade-filtered digests feasible for a solo operator.

candidates.name: Hometown Personalized Gifts on Etsy (Printify, Canadian print providers)
candidates.one_liner: Etsy shop selling personalized Canadian-town/name/date mugs, prints and tote bags, printed and shipped from Canadian Printify providers, with personalization rendered automatically from the Etsy order field.
candidates.target_customer: Canadian gift buyers (moving-away, new-home, hockey-family, cottage) who search Etsy for personalized items shipped domestically without duties.
candidates.problem: Most Etsy POD ships from the US to Canada with slow delivery, duties and CAD/USD confusion; personalized Canadian-specific designs are thin.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Mugs CAD 24-29, 8x10 prints CAD 22-28, totes CAD 29-34; free shipping over CAD 35; personalization included.
candidates.first_10_customers: Etsy search (Canadian-specific long-tail keywords like town names and 'Canada' gifts) plus a small Etsy Ads test (CAD 2-3/day) ahead of Q4 gifting.
candidates.first_100_customers: Expand SKUs across 100+ town/city names and occasions, Pinterest pins of mockups, and Etsy's Q4 traffic (17.2M gross buyer adds in Q4 2025).
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Ships from Canada in 4-8 days in CAD; personalization automated so it can be fulfilled without the owner touching orders.

evidence.claim: Printify with Canadian providers yields 30-50% margins in CAD with 4-8 day Canadian ship times; production 2-7 business days.
Etsy Fall/Winter 2025 seller trend report: shoppers want personalized gifts with a name or date (mugs, wall art).
Real POD margin on Etsy is reduced by listing fees, transaction and payment fees, discounts and offsite ads; experienced sellers price for 40-50%.
Time to first sale for a new shop with 30-50 listings is 2-6 weeks; no median found.

candidates.gross_margin_est: 25-35% net of Printify cost, Etsy fees (6.5% + payment + $0.20 listing) and any ads
candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner opens Etsy and Printify accounts (identity, bank) once; orders flow Etsy -> Printify automatically; occasional buyer messages answered by scheduled runs.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Invisible in Etsy search among millions of POD listings; Q4 window missed if listings are not live by early November.
key_risks: Etsy account suspensions common for new POD shops
Refunds/reprints on personalization errors erode margin
Printify price changes
Etsy Ads spend can exceed early profit
candidates.why_now_2026: Canadian Printify providers now offer 4-8 day domestic delivery and Etsy is explicitly promoting personalization for Q4 2025-2026; cross-border duty confusion pushes Canadian buyers toward domestic sellers.

candidates.name: Canadian Test-Prep Workbooks on Amazon KDP
candidates.one_liner: Paperback medium-content workbooks for Canadian-specific exams (citizenship test practice, provincial driver knowledge tests, Red Seal trade practice questions) published via KDP for Amazon.ca.
candidates.target_customer: Newcomers preparing for the Canadian citizenship test, new drivers by province, and apprentices preparing for Red Seal exams.
candidates.problem: Amazon.ca has few updated, province-specific practice books; most available ones are US-focused or outdated.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Paperbacks CAD 14.99-19.99 (KDP 60% royalty minus print cost ~CAD 4-5); optional Kindle edition CAD 6.99.
candidates.first_10_customers: Amazon.ca organic search for exam-name keywords plus a free companion quiz site linking to the books.
candidates.first_100_customers: A 10-15 book portfolio across provinces/trades, Amazon A+ content, and Kindle Unlimited reads; 100 sales by Day 90 requires a portfolio, not one title.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Current-year Canadian content, province-specific editions and practice-question volume that generic titles lack.

evidence.claim: Most KDP publishers earn $0-$30/month in their first 6 months; a 15-40 book portfolio is needed for $500-$3,000/month.
One low/medium-content publisher reported >$600 royalties in August 2025 from 14 books.
KDP income in year one typically spans $0-$300/month during portfolio validation.
Canadian exam-prep niches on Amazon.ca have lower competition than US equivalents; not verified with keyword tools.

candidates.gross_margin_est: 45-55% of list price after print cost and Amazon's 40% share
candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner creates the KDP account with tax/bank info once; manuscripts, covers and uploads are generated by the operator.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Tiny sales velocity in the first 90 days; KDP payouts are 60 days in arrears so cash lands after the period.
key_risks: KDP AI-content disclosure and quality review may delay or reject titles
Royalties paid ~60 days after month end
Question accuracy liability for exams
Amazon.ca low review count suppresses ranking
candidates.why_now_2026: Record immigration-backlog cohorts and Red Seal demand keep exam searches high while 2025-2026 rule changes date the existing books.

candidates.name: Multi-marketplace passive POD (Redbubble/TeePublic) for niche Canadian humour designs
candidates.one_liner: Upload the same 100-300 designs (Canadian regional humour, trades, hobbies) to marketplace-native POD sites where the platform handles traffic, fulfilment and support.
candidates.target_customer: Casual gift shoppers browsing Redbubble/TeePublic for niche-identity stickers, tees and mugs.
candidates.problem: Niche identity designs are underserved outside the biggest fandoms; buyers want stickers/tees that reference their trade, town or hobby.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Platform-set prices; artist margin set at 20-30% on stickers (USD 2-4), tees (USD 22-28).
candidates.first_10_customers: Marketplace internal search driven by tag-rich listings; no external marketing.
candidates.first_100_customers: Design volume (hundreds of tagged designs) plus Pinterest pins; realistically Day 120+.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Requires no Etsy account, no ads and no customer service; lowest owner involvement of any POD option.

Independent review: Redbubble is a supplementary income stream for artists with an existing audience, not a reliable primary income after 2025 fee changes.
TeePublic/other marketplaces will accept mass uploads of AI-assisted designs without account limits; not verified.

candidates.gross_margin_est: ~50% of artist margin after Redbubble Standard fee; effectively 10-15% of retail
candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner creates accounts and PayPal once; uploads scripted.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: 50% platform fee on Standard tier plus saturated catalogues make Day-90 revenue negligible; included for completeness, not recommended.
key_risks: Platform fee changes
Design takedowns for trademark
Payout thresholds delay cash
Mass low-quality uploads violate the legitimacy rule and platform policy

candidates.lens: NICHE MARKETPLACES, DIRECTORIES, JOB BOARDS, INBOUND LEAD-GEN
candidates.name: HiresCanadians: remote jobs board of roles explicitly open to Canada-based applicants
candidates.one_liner: Aggregates jobs from public Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby boards that state Canada eligibility, then sells featured placements and employer profiles.
candidates.model_type: niche job board (free aggregated listings + paid featured)
candidates.target_customer: Candidate side: Canadian knowledge workers filtering out US-only remote roles; paying side: startups and Canadian employers hiring remote in Canada.
candidates.problem: Remote boards are dominated by US-only listings; Canadians waste time on ineligible roles and employers hiring in Canada struggle to reach them.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Free aggregated listings; CAD 99 featured 30-day listing, CAD 199 featured + newsletter mention, CAD 49/mo employer profile.
candidates.first_10_customers: Employers whose aggregated listings already get clicks are offered an upgrade via the listing page (inbound only); posts in Canadian tech/remote-work communities that allow sharing.
candidates.first_100_customers: SEO on 'remote jobs Canada [role]' pages, a weekly digest newsletter, and recurring employers; 100 paid listings is a Day-180+ outcome.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Eligibility-verified Canadian listings and CAD pricing well below We Work Remotely's $299 per post.

evidence.claim: Real Work From Anywhere passed $5k MRR after 3 years; first paid job listing came in March 2025 with ~99% margin.
Early-stage niche boards charge $99-$199 per listing and manually sell 1-3 listings/month; $1,500-$5,000/mo takes 12-18 months.
We Work Remotely charges $299/post; 15-25% of employers buy premium upgrades when offered at checkout.
Public ATS boards can be aggregated under their terms with attribution; needs per-source checking.

candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner sets up Stripe/domain once; aggregation, eligibility classification (LLM), newsletter and checkout are automated.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Chicken-and-egg: employers will not pay until candidate traffic exists, and traffic takes longer than 90 days.
key_risks: ATS scraping terms
Employer outreach is banned under CASL so upgrades must be strictly inbound
Existing Canadian boards (Jobillico, Indeed) dominate search
Paid listing demand is lumpy
candidates.why_now_2026: Remote-work eligibility confusion peaked as US firms tightened geography; cheap LLM classification makes eligibility filtering feasible for a solo operator.

candidates.lens: NICHE MARKETPLACES, DIRECTORIES, JOB BOARDS, INBOUND LEAD-GEN
candidates.name: Exclusive-lead RFQ site for one trade in one province (e.g., septic pumping / basement waterproofing in Ontario)
candidates.one_liner: A single-trade, single-province quote-request site that delivers each homeowner request exclusively to one contractor who has opted in, priced per lead below HomeStars but without lead sharing.
candidates.target_customer: Small Ontario contractors in one high-ticket, low-competition trade who currently buy shared leads from HomeStars/Angi or rely on word of mouth.
candidates.problem: HomeStars leads are shared with 3-8 contractors, cost C$40-80 plus $200-500/mo, and contractors rate the service 2.7/5 with lock-in contracts.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: CAD 45-75 per exclusive lead billed via Stripe (prepaid credits, no contract); contractors sign up inbound on the site.
candidates.first_10_customers: Contractors arrive via the site's 'get leads' page found through SEO ('exclusive [trade] leads Ontario') and via the homeowner side telling providers where they found them; no cold outreach (CASL).
candidates.first_100_customers: Replicate the template across trades/provinces once one trade converts; 100 contractors is a Day-180+ outcome, but 100 leads sold by Day 90 is plausible with small ad spend.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Exclusive leads, no annual contract, CAD pricing, instant email/SMS delivery; contractors already pay more for worse leads.

evidence.claim: Canadian contractors report C$40-80 per HomeStars lead, annual contracts with 30-35% cancellation penalties; leads shared with 3-8 contractors.
HomeStars subscriptions run $200-$500+/month plus $10-$100 per lead; charged when homeowners shortlist regardless of contact.
HomeStars.ca rated 2.7/5 by 194 customers; BBB complaint history documents contractor dissatisfaction.
A new site can generate 20-40 qualified homeowner requests/month in one trade with SEO plus CAD 150-250 of Google Ads; not verified.

candidates.gross_margin_est: 50-70% after ad spend; 90%+ on organic leads
candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner must open and fund a Google Ads account and Stripe; lead routing, billing and contractor onboarding are automated. Lead disputes may need a monthly 15-minute review.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Homeowner demand side stalls (no organic ranking yet and ads too expensive), so there are no leads to sell in the window.
key_risks: Google Ads cost per homeowner request may exceed lead price
Lead quality disputes/refunds
Contractor acquisition must be strictly inbound under CASL
Seasonality of the chosen trade
candidates.why_now_2026: Contractor frustration with HomeStars/Angi lead sharing and contracts is well documented in 2025-2026, and lightweight LLM lead qualification makes exclusive, verified leads cheap to produce.

candidates.lens: NICHE MARKETPLACES, DIRECTORIES, JOB BOARDS, INBOUND LEAD-GEN
candidates.name: HostedInCanada: directory of SaaS/cloud tools with Canadian data residency, monetized by featured vendor listings
candidates.one_liner: A curated, verifiable directory of software and hosting vendors that store data in Canada, seeded from public docs and monetized with $99/mo featured placements and category sponsorships.
candidates.target_customer: Buyers: Canadian SMBs, clinics, law firms, municipalities and public-sector procurement needing data residency; payers: vendors selling to them.
candidates.problem: Buyers must check each vendor's privacy page for residency claims; vendors with Canadian hosting have no place to stand out on that attribute.
candidates.offer_and_pricing: Free basic listing (seeded); CAD 99/mo featured in category; CAD 299/mo category sponsorship; 'verified residency' badge included with paid tiers after documentation review.
candidates.first_10_customers: Vendors whose free listing page ranks for '[category] Canadian data residency' see the upgrade CTA; inbound only. Communities of Canadian IT/privacy professionals where sharing is allowed.
candidates.first_100_customers: Programmatic category x compliance pages (PIPEDA, PHIPA, Quebec Law 25), a public residency dataset earning links, and vendor referrals; 100 paying vendors is a 12-month goal.
candidates.why_over_alternatives: Only directory verifying residency claims; SaaSHub-style pricing works because vendors' buyer intent is compliance-driven and high-ticket.

evidence.claim: SaaSHub charges $99/month for featured placement and with 108 featured listings exceeds $10k MRR.
OpenAlternative (community directory launched Feb 2023) makes ~$3-3.5k/month; directory sites commonly reach $600-$3,500/mo each.
Vendors will pay CAD 99/mo for a compliance-attribute directory within 90 days of launch; not verified.

candidates.owner_involvement_notes: Owner sets up Stripe/domain once; seeding from public privacy pages, verification checklists and billing are automated.
candidates.biggest_failure_reason: Directory traffic takes longer than 90 days to reach the level at which vendors see value; first paid listing may slip past Day 45.
key_risks: Residency claims must be accurate to avoid misrepresentation
Vendor upgrades must be inbound (CASL)
AI Overviews may answer residency questions directly
Quebec Law 25 nuance requires careful, non-legal-advice framing
candidates.why_now_2026: Quebec Law 25 enforcement, federal privacy reform debate and US data-sovereignty concerns in 2025-2026 make 'is my data in Canada' a live procurement question.
